The strongest honest case is thin. The brief shows 41 buyers and 11.44 SOL bought over the last 15 minutes, against 6.86 SOL sold, so net flow is positive (+4.58 SOL). The coin is alive, 30 minutes old, up 7.65% over 30 minutes, and has a deep pool (705 SOL), which means a $20 ticket would face relatively low impact. Recent buyers outnumber sellers.

But the first two minutes tell the real story: 602.88 SOL bought by 13 buyers, with the top 5 buyers taking 99.9% of it, a launch bot present, and the bundle share at 100%. That is the operator pattern, and the 15-minute flow is small next to that initial concentration. Nothing here shows demand broad enough to survive if the operator exits. The 0.07% sell-to-buy ratio in the opening minutes suggests the operator held, but the brief can't tell us their intent.

I see no case strong enough to buy now. The most I can say is that the coin is not yet visibly collapsing, and the recent flow is modestly positive. Skipping costs nothing; a buy here rides on an operator's future decisions, with fees of 1.4-5.1% already against us. I'd pass.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution by the operator. The first two minutes after graduation show 602.88 SOL bought from 13 wallets, with bundle_share and top3_share both at 1.0 and top5_buyer_share at 0.9991, so the operator's cluster holds nearly all early supply. Sell-to-buy in that window was 0.0007, meaning almost nothing sold while they accumulated. The last 15 minutes flipped to net selling: 6.86 SOL out versus 11.44 in, with 28 sellers against 41 buyers, and the 30-minute return is only +7.65% with a 1.27% last-15 return. That looks like the cluster beginning to exit into retail demand. With a $20 ticket and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, a dip of a few percent wipes the edge, and a cluster unloading 600+ SOL of position would crater the price well past that. Skip.
